sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Conditioned media, membrane, and cytosolic fractions blotted for HA (N-terminal, ectodomain) and Flag (C-terminal, intracellular stub) fragments; surface expression and ectodomain shedding confirmed. Receptor signaling (e.g., VEGF-stimulated phosphorylation) NOT MEASURED in this study.
sites.rationale: FLT1 is a type I single-pass transmembrane receptor with its N-terminus extracellular; the signal peptide spans residues 1–26 (cleavage after G26), so an N-terminal tag must be placed after residue 26 to avoid co-translational cleavage. The paper reports 'N-terminal HA tag' on full-length, membrane-anchored FLT1 with no residue number stated; because exactly one extracellular terminus exists, the junction is unambiguously after the signal peptide cleavage site (insert_after_residue=26, residue_before=G, residue_after=S). Python-verified: residue 26 = G, residue 27 = S, 732 residues from the mature N-terminus to the TM boundary, well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. Full-length FLT1 (HA-VEGFR1-Myc-Flag) expressed in HEK293 cells as a membrane-anchored receptor; N-terminal HA tag placed on the extracellular face, C-terminal Myc-Flag on the intracellular face; construct used to study PMA-stimulated ectodomain cleavage and shedding.

sources.claim: To determine if there were two separate cleavage events we expressed Flt1 with an N-term HA tag and a C-term Flag tag in HEK293 cells and stimulated cleavage with PMA.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) derive from the same paper (PMC4879079) and describe the same dual-tagged construct (HA-VEGFR1-Myc-Flag). L1 is used as the primary supporting clip. The C-terminal Myc-Flag tag (L2) is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for FLT1; no such site is proposed. The N-terminal HA tag position is topology_derived: the paper names no residue number, but FLT1 has exactly one extracellular terminus (after signal peptide cleavage at residue 26), making the junction unambiguous.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Myc-Flag tag on full-length FLT1 (HA-VEGFR1-Myc-Flag construct); the C-terminus lies in the intracellular domain (residues 781–1338) and is not accessible from the extracellular face.
